verdict.floorReached: chain3 (pure depth-3 spine) reached 5 clear-margin flips, IDENTICAL to chain5 (depth-5) at 5 and far above native's 3. So reshape's minimum is 5, NOT native-level (~3). The leafless spine shapes (chain3=5, chain5=5) sit at a constant floor of 5; cutting committed-spine depth 5->3 did not move it. The remaining 5->3 gap (the +2 our-spine-vs-native floor) is the GDN scan state-feed chunk-vs-recurrent realization gap, addressable only by scan-align/WY (parked), not by depth reshape. CAVEAT from post-run research (commits c368bc5f, ec342d86): when re-scored vs a RECURRENT no-spec oracle (instead of the chunked re-prefill frame used by the flip instrument), the spine gap shrinks to ~1 ULP (0.0078 chunked vs 0.000854 recurrent, 9.14x) — so the absolute "+2 floor" magnitude is partly an oracle-frame artifact. Does not change the depth-vs-width verdict (both shapes scored on the same frame).
verdict.coResidencyVerdict: WIDTH adds co-residency flips; it is NOT depth-dominated. cat3w (depth-3 spine + 2 rank-1 leaves: root runner-up (1,) and d1 runner-up (0,1)) = 25 clear-margin flips vs chain3 (same depth-3 spine, zero width) = 5. That is a ~5x jump from adding just 2 leaf nodes to an otherwise identical spine — a clean A/B (same depth, +width only). It mirrors the cat9(22)/chain5(5) ratio. So shallow rank-1 leaf width re-introduces large, real co-residency contamination of spine-0. The two WIDTH shapes (cat3w 25, cat9 22) are both ~5x the two LEAFLESS spine shapes (chain3 5, chain5 5). This is the deployable answer to the crashed A/B: width is the co-residency carrier; depth is not (chain3 5 == chain5 5). NOTE: cat3w's denominator is smaller (total_positions=466, served_lens [86,124,128,128]; prompt0 truncated at 86) vs chain3's 512 — even normalized (5.4% vs 1.0%) the gap stands.
verdict.deployable: No shape is deployable as both flips~native AND accept>=native. Lossless side: the only shapes near the lossless floor are the leafless spines (chain3/chain5 = 5 flips), but 5 > native's 3 and they carry NO leaf width = poor speed (branchless). The deployable (width-bearing) shapes cat3w(25)/cat9(22) are ~5-7x off native on flips = NOT lossless-to-native. So there is NO shape with flips~native that also has accept>=native. ACCEPT is the open gap AND is class-12 cross-boot confounded so no help/hurt conclusion is drawable: RAW accept/event = chain3 2.295, cat3w 2.108, chain5 2.664, cat9_bi 3.109, native E5 1.36..3.154 on different boots. cat3w's 2.108 < chain3's 2.295 in this RAW whole-window delta means width did NOT visibly recover d0/d1 accept here, but that is exactly the cross-boot whole-window trajectory confound the directive flagged (the >=3.16 target is a shifting baseline) — reported raw, not concluded. Net: reshape can hit the lossless-closest spine (still +2 over native, requiring parked scan-align/WY for the last 5->3) OR a deployable-speed width shape (~5x worse flips) — but not both.
verdict.nextAction: Pursue the parked scan-align/WY path (close the GDN scan state-feed chunk-vs-recurrent +2 spine floor, 5->3) — the depth/reshape lever is exhausted for reaching native. FIRST, before committing GPU to WY: re-score the chain5/chain3 spine flips against a RECURRENT no-spec decode oracle (not the chunked re-prefill frame the flip instrument used) per the c368bc5f/ec342d86 finding, to confirm whether the +2 floor is a real kernel wall or an oracle-frame artifact (~1 ULP vs recurrent) — that decides whether WY is even needed.
